# A better compatible heat certificate for the exceptional cubic

The central all-ROC-implies-QC question is still open. This continuation constructs a different leading heat correction and proves the following improvement for the explicit open family in the checkpoint:

\[
 P_\nu=2|X|^2|Y|^2+|Y|^4+\operatorname{Re}(\overline X Y^2)
                  +\nu(|X|^2+|Y|^2)
 \quad\text{is QC whenever}\quad
 \nu\ge\nu_*:=\frac{3+\sqrt3}{24}=0.197168783648703\ldots .
\]

The previous sufficient threshold was 1/4. The exact ROC threshold remains 3/16. Thus the concrete unresolved interval is now

\[
 3/16\le\nu<(3+\sqrt3)/24.
\]

The construction is global in the mean and amplitude and uses actual gradient heat flow. It is not a numerical field test. It also yields a rational certificate at \(\nu=1/5\). The optimized threshold is sharp within the complete class of polynomial heat certificates whose corrected density is a sum of squares of expressions affine in the base gradient and linear in the compatible Hessian; the last part of this report specifies and proves that scope. This is a certificate-class result, not a necessary QC condition.

"""Independent coefficient elimination for the masked result_7535b35 SOS barrier.

Only local SymPy; no imports from author artifacts and no file writes.
Run with python3 -B.  Output is captured beside this file by the reviewer.
"""
import sympy as s
from itertools import combinations, combinations_with_replacement

a,b,c,d = s.symbols('a b c d', real=True)
A=s.Matrix([a,b,c,d]); hv=s.symbols('h0:6', real=True)
h=s.Matrix(hv)
B1=s.Matrix([h[0],h[1],h[3],h[4]])
B2=s.Matrix([h[1],h[2],h[4],h[5]])
T=A.dot(A);D=a*d-b*c
F=3*T*T-4*T*D-4*D*D
X=a+d+s.I*(c-b);Y=a-d+s.I*(c+b)
P=(h[0]-h[2]+2*h[4]+s.I*(h[3]-h[5]-2*h[1]))/4
Q=(h[0]+h[2]+s.I*(h[3]+h[5]))/4
R=(h[0]-h[2]-2*h[4]+s.I*(h[3]-h[5]+2*h[1]))/4
cc=s.conjugate
real=lambda z:s.expand((z+cc(z))/2)
norm=lambda z:s.expand(z*cc(z))
L7=X*Q+2*Y*P
L5=X*R+2*Y*Q
L3=X*cc(R)+2*cc(Y)*P
V=s.Matrix([cc(X)*P+2*cc(Y)*Q,
             Y*cc(R)+X*cc(Q)+cc(Y)*Q,
             X*cc(Q)+2*cc(Y)*Q])
pairs=list(combinations(range(4),2))

def form(degree, name):
    mon=[s.prod(v) for v in combinations_with_replacement(A,degree)]
    coeff=s.symbols(name+':'+str(6*len(mon)), real=True)
    Om=s.zeros(4)
    for row,(i,j) in enumerate(pairs):
        Om[i,j]=sum(coeff[row*len(mon)+k]*m for k,m in enumerate(mon))
        Om[j,i]=-Om[i,j]
    closed=[]
    for i,j,k in combinations(range(4),3):
        expr=s.diff(Om[j,k],A[i])-s.diff(Om[i,k],A[j])+s.diff(Om[i,j],A[k])
        closed.extend(s.Poly(s.expand(expr),*A).coeffs())
    return Om,list(coeff),closed

def density(poly, Om):
    H=s.hessian(poly,A)
    return s.expand(((B1.T*H*B1)[0]+(B2.T*H*B2)[0]+(B1.T*Om*B2)[0])/16)

# All 60 homogeneous quadratic two-form coefficients are free initially.
